findings.description: F-005: the load path taught here and implemented in paint_app.py had zero error handling. Eight malformed-input classes raised uncaught (JSONDecodeError, KeyError x2, TypeError, TclError x3, IndexError, ValueError). Worse, for the TclError class the document had already been replaced and both history stacks cleared before render_document() threw, so the user's drawing was lost, undo could not recover it, and every subsequent action -- including drawing a new shape -- raised. Chapter 15's Debug Lab 12 already teaches json.JSONDecodeError on a corrupt file, so the prerequisite existed.
findings.resolution: Fixed in projects/tkinter/paint-app/paint_app.py and scripts/build_chapter_18.py. Code: added SHAPE_KINDS; Shape.from_dict now validates kind, coordinate count and numeric type, width and colour type, raising ValueError with a specific message; load_from_path parses into a LOCAL list, validates every colour via canvas.winfo_rgb() (the only place that can, since Shape stays Tkinter-free), and replaces self.document / clears history only after the whole parse succeeds, reporting failures via messagebox.showerror across three except groups. Text: new 18.30 section 'А если файл повреждён?' with the safe code, a warning callout 'Сначала разобрать, потом заменять — а не наоборот' describing the exact data-loss cascade, an info callout on why only the canvas can validate a colour, and a new Debug Lab 16 in 18.31 showing the destructive version (page description updated 'Пятнадцать' -> 'Шестнадцать'). Verified: all 16 malformed-input classes now mishandled = 0, drawing preserved every time, app usable afterwards, injection still blocked, valid round-trip still lossless, and the 5 existing tests/test_paint_app_logic.py assertions still pass.
